scan_metadata.analyst_note: Emerging-focus discovery pass for African Grocery Store across the Kansas City MO-KS retail catchment, run on profile mip-ibhnrvhr v2. Vertical and community sources led: the RefugeKC groceries directory was read entry by entry and was the highest-yield vector, supplying owner names, working phone numbers and concrete assortment for storefronts whose platform profiles carry none of it, and exposing three stale citations. An aggregator-mirror sweep surfaced one storefront with no platform profile at all. 30 candidates recorded, of which 20 are routed as emerging prospects; 18 qualifying storefronts are recorded as established reference context rather than prospects. 19 of 118 grid ZIPs were not opened as independent units and are recorded not_executed — coverage is verified_partial, not a census.
scan_metadata.geography_grid_derivation: ZIP set and adjacent municipalities copied verbatim from the cached market grid, which derives them from the Kansas City city boundary plus contiguous incorporated suburbs sharing ZIPs, plus the arterial corridors where category evidence had previously been observed. Sweeps were executed at metro centroid (12z) and corridor centroids (13z-15z) rather than per ZIP; the ledger records that distinction explicitly.
scan_metadata.google_maps_ground_truth: unavailable — the prompt reported no ground-truth signal (level: latest), so corpus fields are marked not_measured rather than inferred. Live Google Maps queries were run directly for this pass and their results are recorded as observed evidence.

scan_metadata.bronze_calibration: Bronze profile mip-wp2mklfs v5 read as the hunt list. Its three live-vector reasons (aggregator_shadow_presence_only, alternate_identity, community_only_no_reviews) were the productive ones in this market; the platform-field-audit reasons filled where a profile carried no website, no phone or no hours. Reasons with empty slots in the bronze block that this pass could have filled — no_website_or_contact, stale_or_missing_hours, zero_or_floor_reviews — are attributed where the profile evidence genuinely matches, and are flagged as such.
scan_metadata.catalog_drift_note: The bronze profile was authored against catalog revision 4; the catalog is now at revision 8. scan_metadata.focus_discipline: Established, mainstream-visible storefronts (Crossland, O The World, Safari Mart, Global Market, Universal Tropical) are retained in the discovery record for identity and category context with business_seek_recommended=false. category_definition: A permanent walk-in food retailer whose physical shelves carry groceries imported from or characteristic of African countries or African diaspora cuisines. Qualification rests on assortment evidence — named products, product-region statements, shelf photography or reported stock — never on the business name, a platform category label, or halal status alone. Subcategories observed here: East African and Somali groceries (Baraka Market, Mogadisho Market, Jubba Valley, Al Halal/Darsalaam, Hilaal, Afro Ethiopia, Fundisha); West African and Ivorian/Ghanaian/Nigerian groceries (Ivoire African Market, Universal Tropical Market, VJ Tropical Market, Ej African Market, Al Rahaman); pan-African and Caribbean hybrids (Crossland International Market, Pan Afro-Caribbean International Market, O The World Tropical Market); and importer-operated retail (Global Market / New Century Imports, Buwen's African Imports). Business models are product retail throughout — a storefront with shelving, a checkout and posted hours. Edge variants: grocery-with-kitchen hybrids (Jay's Grocery & Restaurant, Jubba Valley Market & Kitchen), grocery-plus-goods stores that also sell fabric, shea butter, hair care or clothing (Crossland, Safari Mart, Universal Tropical, Buwen's), and a butcher-and-spice format inside a halal grocery (Barakah Halal Market). Excluded from the qualifying set: restaurants serving African cuisine without retail shelves, African goods stores selling no groceries, halal markets with no African assortment evidence, wholesalers and manufacturers, e-commerce-only operations, and three storefronts the primary platform records as permanently closed.
geographic_classification_notes: inside_city = within Kansas City, MO limits. adjacent_city = an immediately contiguous incorporated municipality in the same retail catchment: Gladstone (shares ZIP 64118), Riverside, Independence, Grandview, Raytown, and Kansas City, KS. metro_area = the broader catchment across the state line: Overland Park, Olathe, Shawnee, Lenexa. No candidate fell outside_market within the 25-mile radius. The observed geography is two dense clusters plus scattered nodes. Independence Avenue (64106/64124) holds 10 qualifying storefronts within roughly a mile — Baraka, Ej, Hilaal, Jay's, Al Halal, Al Rahaman, Huda Food, Mogadisho, Pichenafrican, and Crossland at the City Market end. North Oak Trafficway (64118/64116) holds 5 African storefronts — Universal Tropical, African Market Universal Tropical, African International Market, Tour of Africa and Barakah Halal Market — plus the Haitian store the directory surfaced and Afro Ethiopia on NW Vivion in Riverside. Single-storefront nodes: Ivoire (Wornall/Waldo), VJ Tropical (Troost), Pan Afro-Caribbean (Grandview), O The World (Raytown), Buwen's (Independence), Global Market (Overland Park), Safari Mart (Olathe), Fundisha (Shawnee), Sankofa and Anointed (KCK), Banadir (St John Avenue). The Lee's Summit / Blue Springs / Grain Valley sweep executed empty. City Market is a comparator node, not an African-grocery concentration in its own right. Two additional storefronts sit inside the Independence Avenue cluster but are not counted because they could not be verified as current: the Somali Mall's unnamed meat and food mart tenant, and Holy Land Market at the mall address.
ownership_exclusion_notes: No national chain, national franchise or multi-state regional chain qualified — the category is structurally independent in this market, and the observed roster is owner-operated single storefronts plus two small local groups. Universal Tropical Market LLC and African Market Universal Tropical Market are local_chain: two storefronts on N Oak Trafficway within two miles, with reviews naming the same owner ('AJ') and describing 'several store locations'. Global Market / New Century Imports is local_chain: one Overland Park retail storefront plus a wholesale distribution arm and a Wichita branch documented on the owned site — a single-metro independent importer, not a regional retail chain. Breadth-based exclusions are listed in excluded_out_of_category_or_market: broad international grocers (World Fresh Market, 888 Int'l Market), a Mediterranean market (Kanza), South Asian halal grocers (Pak Halal), Afghan and Arab markets (Afghan Market, ALNAJIB, Aswaq Al Arabi), African goods stores selling no groceries (Africa 2000, Building BLACC, Sharif Store), a wholesaler (One Stop Store), a spice manufacturer (Spicin Foods), a convenience/food-service hybrid (5709 Market), and three permanently closed storefronts (Aboom Tropical Market, Karibu Store, and — recorded as a lead because its owned site is live — Arada Market). One-Stop Shop Haitian Store is retained in the discovery record with category_fit insufficient and hold status: Haitian cuisine is Caribbean rather than African, and the platform carries a Caribbean Grocery Store shelf for that business.

platform_analysis.note: Gold-standard gates are recorded as an opportunity map for emerging routing, not as a selection filter. In this focus a failed gate is a fixable visibility gap, and gold_standard_match is deliberately not used to rank prospects.

outreach_recommendation.platform_rationale: Google is where the gap is both largest and cheapest to close. Every emerging prospect here already has a live profile, so the work is correction rather than creation: 18 of the 20 recommended prospects publish no owned website, 17 carry a generic or wrong primary category, and 6 publish no hours block at all. No other platform carries enough of the category's prospects to justify leading elsewhere — Yelp holds six of thirty and Facebook three.

outreach_recommendation.primary_angle: Identity and category correction before anything else: the Independence Avenue cluster is a genuine African and halal grocery district where several storefronts are invisible under their own name — one unit trades under four names, another under two addresses — so the first win is making each store findable under the name on its own sign.

suggested_signals.proposed_definition: Three or more trading names resolve to a single street unit and phone number across platform, community and directory sources, usually reflecting a succession of owners or licences. No single name search reaches the business, and each name carries a fragment of the true review, hours and category picture.
exemplar_leads: Al Halal Grocery Store (Al Halal / Darsalaam / Tawakal / Maka)

suggested_signals.proposed_label: Owned site contradicts platform closure status
suggested_signals.proposed_definition: The business's own domain publishes hours and contact details while the primary platform records the location as permanently closed. One of the two is wrong; until it is resolved the storefront cannot be safely treated as operating or as closed.

suggested_signals.proposed_label: Community directory cites a closed storefront
suggested_signals.proposed_definition: A community or refugee-services directory still lists a grocery as operating after the primary platform marked it permanently closed. Directory-derived discovery therefore carries closed storefronts forward as live prospects unless every entry is status-checked.
